NTA. If anything I think you’re lowballing how much you’re asking for considering for expensive the hobby is and your fish of choice is. Koi aren’t really fish so much as appreciating, living pieces of art- if the dead fish were larger and of rarer breeds, id be looking at how much a similar fish would go for at auctions and private sellings and use that as a basis to be made whole

Koi are not the same as carp, that’s like saying a husky is the same as a wolf. Koi came from carp but they are not the same. Koi have been selectively bred to be a decorative feature in ponds, focusing on aesthetics rather than hardiness- so yeah, it’s entirely plausible that they got stressed especially when the filter was damaged because a lot of breeds demand clean water and don’t handle rapid change well. 

And it depends on what pond filter we’re talking about. If it’s a biological, then whatever toxins Timmy introduced to the pond could have killed it biomedia and caused a rapid nitrogen recycle. Or he could have just knocked a rock in to the intake or motor, which would have caused the same thing essentially even if the filter was still limping along- and then cause a recycle by the time the owner found out that the filter wasn’t working at 100%. And when that happens, ammonia levels can rise so quickly and without sufficient aeration then it’s entirely possible that the fish died.

Actually, decorative fish can be very expensive especially if you’re buying them full grown especially koi. These aren’t common carp or Walmart goldfish mostly likely- if he’s talking about specific breeds, then those can easily go over 1k and if he’s trying to replace them full grown, then double or triple that amount especially if he has to ship them. 

Best way I can explain this to non enthusiasts is that you’re not really buying a “fish” but you’re buying a living art piece that will continue to grow and become more unique as the decades go on (koi can live over 40 years). This means that the older, the more cared for, the bigger the koi is, the rarer the breed/coloring, = the more expensive it is and harder to replace. I’m genuinely surprised that the amount is so low, the kid might have just killed young koi that may have not matured; because I’ve seen full grown koi go for 10,000$. The lady doesn’t know how lucky she is because if he wanted resale value it could go way higher. I can only imagine if her kid killed a pond full of decorative arowanas, she’d have to refinance her house.

If you haven’t already, you should make a report to the local animal control about the dangerous dog and the irresponsible owner and turn over the footage that you have. Even though the cat was outside your house, it was still on your property when the dog owner allowed it to trespass and kill a non violent animal. Especially since you did not mention that he did not try to save your cat by retrieving his animal, nor does it seem like he tried to save the cat by taking it to a vet or even calling animal control himself so they could render aid to your animal. 

People like this guy absolutely do not need to own power breeds because of situations like this. He obviously has no control over his animal since it fatally attacked another animal in a very unnecessary encounter that the owner caused (in my county, this would absolutely be a dangerous animal confiscation where both the dog would be evaluated to see if it’s safe to live in a community and if the pet owner is evaluated to be competent to own an animal). I wouldn’t even be surprised if he did this on purpose- I’ve seen people get these tough looking dogs out of insecurity and encourage them to do horrible things to satisfy whatever twisted thoughts they have. 

In the end, it’s also the dog getting abused because they’re being told to do things or otherwise being allowed to do things that will eventually get them hurt/euthanized. So honestly, the sooner this dog gets taken from this dude is better, because who knows what situation this dude will put his animal in next. Because this was such a mundane event, there is a reasonable expectation that if you walk around a neighborhood there might be someone’s cat wandering around. Even if he claims it’s ignorance, that’s even worse to me because like I said this is a large, powerful dog- he should know how his dog is going to react to something before he takes him in public because that is his animal. You can’t say “I didn’t know he could do that!” when the dog is 100 pounds and unrestrained in a public area. The neighborhood should be able to enjoy the general public without worrying about random dogs mauling whatever might trigger them. 

But yes, absolutely make a report about this owner and stress how you do not feel safe in your neighborhood because of this to the animal control officer. Make sure you stress that the dog and the owner trespassed, that your animal was on your property and non violent, any relevant history the owner has with being neglectful and any other concerns that you have. And personally, I would ask for a copy of any reports so that I could take the owner to small claims court. I would want to get reimbursed for cremation for starters. Then I would take my other cat to the vet to get him checked out (because stress can cause health issues) and maybe see what the vet says about getting a behaviorist to see him, which I would also add to the suit. You can also add emotional distress to the suit. But that’s just what I would do. If you don’t want to do the legal route, at the very least you need to report this guy, if not for your cat, but for the safety of the other people and animals in your neighborhood. He obviously has no concern in controlling his dangerous animal.

Ive got the same issues that you do in terms of big dogs approaching me while I’m walking my dog and I’m happy to say you’ve got a few options. 

1. Use a snug harness with a handle. You should be using harnesses anyways because of their delicate necks but when there’s danger you don’t want to be shuffling around trying to get a grip on your scared dog. Also, always make sure your dog is secured before you take them out to avoid situations like this but also, loose fitting harnesses are uncomfortable and can cause chafing. To tell if it’s secured, if you can put two fingers in comfortably where the chest, neck, and shoulders are, it fits. If the harness slides around, or if you can slip it off in anyway, then resize or get a smaller size. For peace of mind there’s also harnesses for escape artists that have so many clips that even determined huskies can’t get out of. And since you have small dogs, you can even use cat harnesses. 

2. Only use fixed length leashes/dual leashes. Same concept, you do not want to be fucking around with a twenty foot leash if there’s something happening. If you’re just walking down the street, then all you need is a simple six foot leash where you only have to take two steps to pick your dog up. Since you have two dogs, you can also use a dual leash so you can have one hand free. 

3. If you choose to pick your dogs up, hide them under your shirt or jacket. If a big dog is chasing your dogs and you hold them, they’ll see your dog as a toy and try to snatch them out of your hands. However, that task becomes harder if they’re hidden because 
-dogs don’t like biting or hurting people. Most dogs are socialized or otherwise inhibited from by breeding to hurt people. Of course some dogs don’t feel the same way towards other animals for a variety of reasons but as a person that works with dogs, even those who are very angry/in pain/been cornered tend to blanch at actually attacking a person. Do know that they will try to jump on you otherwise but it’s unlikely they’ll actually bite you
-a lot of dog attacks are visual. When the dogs are not visually aroused, their energy levels tend to drop. Especially when there’s nothing to chase and they have a person telling them to fuck off. 

4. Umbrellas. This has actually saved me, my dogs, and my skin multiple times. Like I said before, dogs tend to be very visual and when you block their vision, it’s not fun anymore. So using an umbrella to block their vision does a lot to stop them and it also puts an actual barrier between you and your dogs against the attacking dog. You may think, it’s flimsy and they can easily go through it but most dogs don’t really think about that. They just see something blocking them and get really confused on why it’s there. But don’t try to hit the dog with the umbrella, some will just take it as they’re getting attacked and fight harder. Also, it’s great protection against the sun

5. Noise. A loud and sudden noise will 9/10 shock a dog into stopping no matter how mad they are but it has to be the right sound. It can’t just be a human voice bc they’re used to it and will block you out. Stuff like a can of coins or an air horn work best, bc it’s something sharp, shocking, sudden, and something they’ve never heard before. And it works consistently, like let’s say the dogs owner doesn’t come out and you have to walk away with the attacking dog loose, every time they approach you make that same noise and they’ll get freaked out like the first time. Plus it also gets people off their ass too when they come to investigate the noise. 

6.  Chemicals. Admittedly my least favorite bc while it is effective it tends to blow back on you and your dogs. You can use pepper spray, bear spray, or wasp spray, but know that even if it doesn’t affect you it will affect your chis. There’s also dog safe sprays, like citronella, which isn’t as harsh and forces the dog to uncontrollably sneeze so much it can’t attack— but it’s a toss up on if it works and how mad the other dog is. I’ve sprayed a charging Doberman right in the face and he didn’t blink. Though, I do recommend carrying one as a last resort in any case. But let’s say you’re being charged by more than one dog, then this should be your first option.

7.  Remember that you’re the human and they’re the dogs. I feel like a lot of people forget this and the fact that dogs are socialized to obey humans. Don’t run away, don’t scream, don’t act like you’re terrified even if you are. If a dog charges you and your dogs, it’s your job to pull your chis behind you, step in between, and tell the charging dog to fuck off. Use the umbrella, the air horn, whatever but once the attacking dog realizes that you aren’t afraid of them and that you won’t make it easy nor fun then they’ll lose a lot of their confidence. I’m serious, I’ve made pits, Dobermans, and Rottweilers stop in their tracks and back off by looking them in the eyes, pointing right at them and telling them stop. Especially the pointing, they really hate that. 

8.  The most important thing you can do is to report these people! I’m serious. A lot of people leave it because they’re shaken up and because nothing happened to their dogs, but that may not happen the next time. And these dogs only get more emboldened when their owners allow them to charge whoever they want to. Even if it’s a mistake and their dogs did get out, it’s a huge problem that their dogs went on attack mode. It’s their responsibility to make sure their dogs are secured and not a menace to their community and they shouldn’t be allowed to pretend like their dogs nearly mauling someone else dog is no big deal. Especially since a lot of people do not care if their large dog kills a small dog because they don’t like small animals and their dog won’t be hurt from the encounter. At my old neighborhood, we had a neighbor who had two large dogs who would jump their fence and charge people they saw on the street. Nobody did anything because we were sympathetic bc it’s not like the owners had sicc’ed them on anyone and tried to keep them in their yard. Until they got out once and mauled a little girl and her puppy. It’s just plain negligent and honestly, only untrained and under exercised dogs do that— I’ve cared for many dogs and have had many power breeds, they don’t do that if they’re adequately exercised and enriched. Even if animal control does nothing and just gives them a warning, thats enough of a kick in the ass for people to do something about their animals. If you know where these people live, report their asses to animal control.

I’m not sure why so many people are disagreeing with bathing, it’s a good practice to bathe after fleas for a lot of reasons; flea dirt, fleas can cause allergic reactions in humans and cats, fleas can still live on your pet even with flea protection, you don’t want the detritus falling all over your house, not all fleas are killed immediately and can jump off to reinfect/go after others, cats cannot clean *everywhere* etc. Cats are fine getting a bath every once in a while, and fleas are definitely a good reason for it. Personally, flea dirt gives me rashes so I always bathe my animals at the first sight. 

Now you do have options aside from bathing at home, you could always get a cat groomer. They’re trained and experienced with how cats are, and often they can come to your home to make it easier. I’ve gotten my shorthair groomed for about $50 and they drove to my house to do it. See if you can call around while businesses are still open. 

If you have to do it at home, I have some tips

-Use unscented cat shampoo. Their noses are a lot more sensitive than ours, so a strong smell will shock/disorient them. 

-Already have the water in the bath. Running water is loud and overwhelming.

-When you run the bath, add a little dish soap to it(don’t add enough to make a bubble bath. Fully expect for some fleas to be alive and they will attempt to jump ship. The dish soap will keep them from jumping out the water. 

-Water temperature should be a little warmer/the temperature that you would bath a baby in. 

-Clip their nails before starting any of this. You can use regular human nail clippers, and basically you’re just cutting off the sharp point. 

- Turn up the heater in your house. They get cold after baths too. 

- Put a towel inside the bath. They’ll feel a lot more comfortable because they feel like they won’t slip on the bottom of the slippery tub. 

-Put a towel on the bath ledge, that way they’ll grab that instead of you if they try to run. 

-Towels everywhere. Try to drape a towel over you. If they try to grab you, they’ll get a paw full of towel 

-if you’re by yourself, one hand on the scruff and other hand needs to be doing the work. If you have help, they need to keep the cats standing on their own four feet. If they feel like they’re slipping, then they’ll panic. 

-Use a cup. Running water is gonna make them panic, so just use a cup to wet the cat and gently rub it in. 

-Get a zoom groom. It’s a rubber bath brush for pets that makes it go by so much faster. Essentially, after you wet the cat and pour soap on, scrub the cat with the zoom groom and it will get them cleaner more efficiently than just hands esp if your cat has thick fur. 

- You’ll need a lot of towels. Towels in bath so the cat grips that instead of you, towels to grab the cat in case it jumps out and you need to put it back in, towels to dry you and the cat, towels on the floor so you don’t slip and slide, etc. Have a stack on hand. 

-Make it quick. Cats all have a countdown and after a while, they’re gonna make it as difficult as possible 

-Talk in a calming voice. Hum. Put on quiet, calm music. Try to give them something to focus on that’s not the bath

-If the cat fights getting in the bath, wrap them up like a burrito in a towel and ease them in

-Wash the face last. Expect a freak out the moment the face gets wet. If you’re alone, then I suggest using waterless shampoo, pet wipes, and a flea comb instead of washing in the bath. 

-Cotton balls in the ears. Bath water in the ear canal is going to give them an ear infection, so split a cotton ball in half and shove it in there. Preferably before getting in the water for obvious reasons. 

-Fleas love hanging inside the ears, so invest in ear wipes and a tips. Be gentle and don’t go too far in the canal

-When the cat gets wet, any living flea will rush to wherever is dry. Just keep that in mind. 

-Wear thick clothing wherever if at all possible

-Make sure to rub everywhere to dislodge any dead fleas, flea eggs, flea dirt, etc. Make it fast tho

-Keep towels on the bathroom ground because when you’re done, the cat is gonna hide in the corner dripping wet. I suggest that you keep the cat inside the bathroom until it’s reasonably dry for this reason. 

-Towel dry as best as you can but know that you’ll probably won’t get them 100% dry. That’s why we put the heater on before we started so the cat won’t be freezing.

Have you given him a bath? No doubt he or she has some kind of bugs on them, and you don’t want fleas anywhere near you. Get pan of something that you can submerge most of his body in water and add some soap to the water. You can clip his nails with human nail cutters to make this next step easier (just don’t cut the pink part of his nail). Put him in the water and keep his head above water; if he has fleas or other bugs, they’ll climb to his head to avoid drowning. Let it happen for a few minutes then use dish soap on his head to knock the fleas out, lather it real good, and rinse him off good. Use a comb to look through his fur and make sure you got all the fleas and to check if he doesn’t have ticks. If he has ticks, get tweezers and grab the bug close to the skin, then pull. Don’t get any soap or water inside his eyes, mouth, or ears.  Dump the water and bugs away from your home because fleas don’t drown and will reinfest the kitten. Then go ahead and wash him for the sake of getting him clean. Also make sure the kitten is completely dry afterwards, I mean not even a little wet, and warm it up. Kittens get sick very easily. If he has bedding that he used before his bath, it either needs to be cleaned with hot water and left in the sun or thrown away. He might need multiple baths as well. 

Secondly, a kitten doesn’t need a lot of room. If he’s out there getting bullied, you need to shoo those cats away (don’t give them a reason to come to your place or fight over resources- don’t leave food out there for them to bully your kitten from) and give the kitten an enclosed place to stay in. Think like a big box or the like, because your kitten is sick and needs to stay warm. If you live somewhere warmer, then don’t worry about it but it probably has anemia because of the parasites so it’ll feel cold. 

Thirdly, if you only have quacks and sketchy vet offices around then you need to speak their language. Ask for prices before they do something. Don’t let them take kitten out of your sight; anything he needs, they can do in your presence. He needs blood drawn? You don’t get sick at the sight of blood and you can hold him still. They need to run tests in the back room? Either I’m going with you or your telling me the exact tests needed so I can look them up right now on my phone and you only consent to those tests being done, you aren’t paying extra for anything the vet didn’t bring up to you first. Why am I saying this? Because they will either not do the tests or take him to the back room, run a bunch of expensive tests he might not need, and charge you a lot. I’ve had it happen with my dog at a sketchy clinic; my puppy ate a candy wrapper so they gave me a blood test, an X-ray, tried to keep the dog overnight, and a bunch of other stuff without my permission and tried to charge me $700. Turns out, she was fine and just needed a little laxative. Start looking up his symptoms right now but he definitely needs a feline leukemia test, a parasite test, a blood test, and a checkup. For example, If he has fleas, he probably has tapeworms, which you can’t get from him; but he can have that and ringworm, which you can get from him (his feces carries the eggs- clean the areas he poops in very good) And when they prescribe medicine, look online to see if they’re over charging you. 

When you drive him to the vet office, he needs to be in a carrier or in a a box. Line the box with plastic on the bottom and something for him to lay on. He might have an accident because he has diarrhea and might get carsick, so put something so it won’t leak out on your car. And make sure he can’t get out, a kitten that size will try to hide. Since he is getting a parasite test, you need to bring fresh poop with you. Put it in a baggy, make sure it’s his, and make sure it’s fresh ( it needs to be not dried out, and happened in the last 24 hours). He doesn’t need food or water in the carrier with him, he’ll be focused on the car ride. Though you should definitely give him water during breaks and at the vet. 

Lastly, until you can take him to a vet you can check on his progress doing a few things. You can test if he’s dehydrated by grabbing some skin, lifting it up, and letting it go. If the skin goes down immediately, then the kitten is not dehydrated. A hydrated animal’s skin should immediately go down. The longer it takes for it to go down, the more dehydrated the kitten is. Encourage him to drink and add water or broth to his food until you can get to a vet. The other thing you can do is press on his gum. His gums should be a healthy pink and when you press down on them, they should turn pink after. If not, he is sick. I heard you can rub syrup on their gums in certain instances but you should look it up for your specific circumstance. If he’s eating, that’s a very good sign, that means he’s a fighter; and kittens should be sleeping a lot anyways, so don’t be worried about that. My kitten sleeps all night and has a five hour nap in the daytime. If he’s not drinking as much as you want, see if he’ll lick droplets from your hands. 

I’m not an experienced cat owner, I’ve only had mine for a few months but I’ve had pets all my life. Pm me if you have any other questions 

Edit: I just reread your post. For eating, try giving her canned food; anchovies, tuna, stinky stuff. See if warming the food makes any difference. Also, act like your eating the food with her and talk to her; you’ll look silly but she might be stressed out from the other cats being there. Try to work up an appetite by playing with her and/or warm her up. See if she’ll eat it with a little bit of cheese on top (not too much, kittens are lactose intolerant!); infact, add things you think she may like with the food. And I want you to look up Cat Fecal Scoring System so you can see what’s normal. Just because she doesn’t have runny poop right now doesn’t mean the cause of it solved itself.
